title: Founder-scale hire: 30d stewardship & shadow plan
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, actionable plan for hiring and onboarding a high-velocity, founder-scale IC (senior PM / eng-lead style hire) where early autonomy + cross-functional stewardship is expected within 30 days.

Intended audience:
- People Ops (recruiting + onboarding)
- Hiring manager (product / eng lead)
- Assigned mentor / steward

Why this document exists (context):
We frequently hire roles that need to ramp into cross-team ownership quickly. Traditional 90-day playbooks are too slow for these hires. This is a blended artifact: hiring criteria + interview rubric + 30-day activation sprint + access and mentor rotation plan.

High-level goals (30 day outcomes):
- Candidate is operationally productive on 1 small cross-team deliverable (spec, migration plan, PoC) within first 21 days.
- Candidate completes a stakeholder map + comms plan and has 1 synchronous demo at day 21.
- Manager can make a confident eval on long-term fit (signal on autonomy, technical judgment, cross-functional influence) by day 30.

Hiring plan summary (timeline):
- Week -4 to -2: Role brief + targeted sourcing (founder references prioritized).
- Week -2 to 0: Screen -> take-home (calibrated to 6–10 hours) -> onsite loop (2.5–3 hrs).
- Offer + acceptance -> preboarding packet (access requests, high-level 30d sprint outline).

Interview rubric (single-page, for loop interviewers):
Scoring: 1–4 (1 = fail/misfit, 4 = exceptional/clear fit). Must have at least two 3+ areas to continue to on-site.

Core dimensions:
- Product/technical sense (can translate tradeoffs, writes clear spec): 1..4
- Systemic judgment (prioritization across infra, cost, latency): 1..4
- Collaboration & influence (stakeholder handling, conflict resolution): 1..4
- Speed & bias for action (delivers minimal viable solution quickly): 1..4
- Learning agility (adapts to unknowns, asks high-quality questions): 1..4
- Culture & role alignment (mission fit, ethics, communication style): 1..4

Signal examples per dimension (short cheat sheet):
- Product/technical: ask candidate to sketch a minimal migration plan for moving an inference workload from single-GPU to autoscaled pods. Look for clarity, risk isolation, rollback plan.
- Systemic judgment: give two competing requests (latency vs cost) and ask how to measure and decide. Accept pragmatic metrics (p50/p95 cost per token).
- Collaboration: ask for a time they changed a partner's mind without authority. Look for framing, evidence, and follow-up.
- Speed: time-box an exercise where candidate produces an outline for a 2-week pilot.

Take-home assignment (purpose-built):
- Keep it to 6–10h. Provide a single narrative plus one artifact (diagram/spec).
- Prompt: "Design a rollout plan to pin a model version across Dedicated and Hosted routes while allowing automatic fallback. Identify failure modes and propose observability probes."
- Evaluation rubric: clarity of steps, rollback strategy, metrics for success, cost controls.

Preboarding checklist (actionable, to be sent upon offer acceptance):
- Welcome note from manager + 30d sprint doc (this file minimalized).
- Slack accounts + channel invites: #team, #oncall-orbit, #people-ops-buddy.
- Accesses requested (see matrix below) — request these immediately after offer accepted.
- Calendar blocks day 1 + week 1 orientation + 1:1 cadence.

Access matrix (request template for infra/product hires) — mark status in preboard:
- Google Workspace: basic (yes)
- Confluence read + edit (yes)
- GitHub: triage (repo list provided)
- AWS/GCP: read-only then escalate to dev/test; ephemeral keys for PoC (manager approval)
- Dedicated console (redwood): dev-route access + view logs
- PagerDuty: not by default; mentor observes first on-call

Mentor & steward rotation (reduces single-point failure):
- Week 0–1: Primary mentor = manager (daily 30m), Secondary mentor = platform-eng (2x 1hr).
- Week 2: Rotate to cross-functional steward (product manager) for 1 week to shadow stakeholder meetings.
- Week 3–4: Introduce rotational pairing with SRE/serving-runtime for technical deep dives (2 sessions).
- Mentor responsibilities: unblock access, review first spec, join first stakeholder demo.

30-day activation sprint (recommended cadence)
- Day 0: orientation, kit, meet team, prioritize first deliverable.
- Days 1–3: small scoped discovery + setup (env, access, hello world run). Owner: new hire.
- Days 4–10: deliverable alpha — draft spec + short PoC. Mentor does daily sync until alpha.
- Days 11–17: stakeholder feedback loop, iterate on alpha, write rollout checklist.
- Days 18–21: demo to stakeholders, collect acceptance signals.
- Days 22–30: finish acceptance items, handoff, manager assessment & growth plan.

Acceptance signals (what manager looks for at day 30):
- Deliverable shipped to internal staging / demo'd.
- Clear evidence of owning cross-team communication (changelog, decision log).
- Positive feedback from at least two partners (eng + product).
- Demonstrated ability to identify one measurable metric to track (latency, cost, success-rate).

Onboarding checklist (quick, non-exhaustive):
- Accounts created + verified
- Local dev environment: hello-world end-to-end within 48h
- First PR created (label: newbie/first-pr)
- Document created: 30d deliverable spec + decisions log
- Intro meetings: infra, product, SRE, RD (20–30m each)
- Security briefing: sensitive data handling + Private deployment basics

Interview red flags (stop criteria):
- Candidate cannot describe a rollback or revert strategy for a real deployment.
- Unable to reason about tradeoffs between latency and cost with concrete metrics.
- Repeatedly blames org/people without responsibility/accountability examples.

Green flags (accelerate offer):
- Presents a crisp one-page plan during onsite that anticipates 2 failure modes.
- Demonstrates a prior instance where they influenced a cross-functional decision and shipped.

Open questions / TODOs (work-in-progress):
- Calibrate take-home: target 6h, but recruiters report 8–12h; update instructions to tighten scope.
- Create invite template for steward rotation (people-ops to own).
- Build a simple Confluence template for 30d sprint that auto-populates manager, mentor, deliverable.

Notes to recruiter/hiring manager (practical):
- Prefers referrals from founders / early-stage PM/ENG leads. Practical evidence > CV.
- Interviewers must submit scored rubric within 48h of interview. No score = automatic follow-up.
- If candidate accepts, send preboard within 24h (includes access checklist + 30d sprint outline).

Appendix (sample interview prompts):
- "You have a deployed model that customers are suddenly querying at 4x baseline. Cost is spiking and p95 latency is slightly worse. Walk me through first three actions you take in the next 24 hours."
- "Sketch a minimal observability plan to detect model-quality regressions post-deploy. What signals would you collect?"

End of doc — this is intended as a pragmatic canvas, not canonical policy. Please comment inline with real examples or updates.

Working notes: Jonah to test take-home on two recent candidates by 2025-07-10; Priya to draft steward rotation invite.
